newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Indonesia criticised over East Timor at UN forum.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia criticised over East Timor at UN forum.

text.p: The world's supreme human rights body formally criticised Indonesia on Wednesday in a resolution expressing deep concern at reports of killings and torture in East Timor, invaded by Jakarta's troops in 1975.
The resolution was the second on Indonesian human rights violations in East Timor since 1993. Last year, Indonesia got away with a less embarrassing chairman's statement at the forum.

The 53-member U.N. Human Rights Commission said it was deeply concerned by continuing reports of violations including extrajudicial killings, disappearances, torture, arbitrary detentions and extrajudicial executions in East Timor.

In a resolution adopted by 20 votes to 14 against and 18 abstentions -- mainly from developing countries but including Japan and Russia -- it called on the government of Indonesia to take measures to ensure respect for the rights of the East Timorese.
The resolution followed intense lobbying in Geneva by East Timor's independence activist and Nobel Peace laureate Jose Ramos Horta.

Horta presented a video to U.N. investigators, diplomats and activists in Geneva purporting to show torture of East Timorese youths by Indonesia's army, full of graphic images including young men nailed to prison planks.

Horta, co-winner of the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize with Bishop Carlos Filipe Ximenes Belo, said the pictures had been smuggled out of the island recently and that he believed they were genuine. Indonesia dismissed them as nonsense and said they were false.
The U.N. forum also urged Jakarta to release East Timorese political detainees, cooperate with U.N. rights investigators and provide the U.N. human rights office with unhindered access to East Timor.
Indonesia annexed the former Portuguese colony in 1976, a year after it invaded the territory just after Portugal pulled out. The annexation has not been recognised by the United Nations.
